attempts.narrative: T1 I led both Ground bodies precisely so the authored Discharge activation could fire for free - and it never came. Electrode spent the turn on Taunt into a Nidoqueen whose four moves are all attacks, Electivire's Ice Punch (2x) took Nidoking to 14, and my two Earth Powers removed Electivire outright; the second one redirected onto Electrode and its Focus Sash left it on 1. T2 Electrode Protected away the Earth Power that would have finished it, my Flamethrower (2x) popped Magnezone's Air Balloon and took it to 28, and Magnezone's Flash Cannon KO'd Nidoking. T3 Magearna replaced it and immediately showed switch_blocked_by: ability_prevents_escape from Magnet Pull; Aura Sphere (2x on Steel) removed Magnezone and Earth Power finally removed Electrode. T4 Thundurus took a Nasty Plot to +2 while Manectric Protected, and my Thunderbolt aimed at Thundurus was pulled into Manectric by Lightning Rod and then blocked by that same Protect - a double-payoff guard. T5 Thundurus threw its whole +2 Life Orb turn into a Thunderbolt that its own partner's Lightning Rod absorbed, and Ice Beam plus Fleur Cannon removed it. T6 Galvantula arrived and correctly used Energy Ball (2x) rather than a useless Thunder into a Ground type, Manectric finally Mega Evolved and its Intimidate dropped Nidoqueen's Attack on the spot, and Mega Manectric's Flamethrower plus that Energy Ball KO'd Magearna. T7 Weavile replaced it, Ice Shard removed the 10 HP Galvantula, Mega Manectric's Flamethrower (2x) KO'd Weavile and Earth Power (2x) closed on the Mega.

ai_defects.board: Thundurus at 94/94, Life Orb, +2 Sp.Atk from its own Nasty Plot the turn before. Its partner was Manectric with Lightning Rod, un-Mega'd, at 88/88. My actives were Nidoqueen (Poison/Ground, 122 HP, Assault Vest - immune to Electric) and Magearna (Steel/Fairy, 116 HP, Assault Vest - resists Electric at 0.5x).
ai_defects.chosen: MOVE_THUNDERBOLT targeting b2 (Magearna). The decision record shows the target was my Pokemon, not its own ally, so this was not a deliberate feed.
ai_defects.why_wrong: Lightning Rod on its own partner guaranteed the attack would never reach Magearna. The log reads 'The opposing Thundurus used Thunderbolt! / The opposing Manectric took the attack! / The opposing Manectric's Sp.Atk rose!'. A +2 Life Orb turn produced zero damage and handed its partner a single Sp.Atk stage. Worse, Thunderbolt was the one move on the set that could not work against that board at all - 0x into Nidoqueen, 0.5x into Magearna, and redirected in practice.
ai_defects.better: MOVE_GRASS_KNOT into Nidoqueen. Grass is 2x on Ground, Nidoqueen is heavy enough to take a high base power, and at +2 with a Life Orb that is a serious hit on the Pokemon that went on to win the battle. Thunder Wave through Prankster was also strictly better than nothing.
ai_defects.generalization: This is an ally-ability blind spot in target scoring, not a Thundurus problem: the scorer did not subtract the value of an Electric attack that its own side's Lightning Rod will intercept. The affected shape is any team that pairs an Electric attacker with a Lightning Rod ally. Inside this block Wattson is the worst case - Manectric's Lightning Rod sits beside five Electric attackers (Electrode, Electivire, Magnezone, Thundurus, Galvantula), so any of them can lose a turn this way. The mirror-image cases are NOT defects and must not be swept into the same fix: Motor Drive (Kirk's Emolga), Volt Absorb (Ben's Lanturn, Shawn's Jolteon) and Dry Skin (Ben's Heliolisk) are authored safe pairings where the friendly hit is the point. The distinction the scorer needs is that Lightning Rod and Storm Drain steal the attack and deny the damage, whereas Volt Absorb, Motor Drive and Dry Skin only absorb what was going to hit the ally anyway. I did not touch AI C code.

ai_defects.board: T1 my actives were Nidoqueen and Nidoking, both Poison/Ground with four attacking moves each and no status move between them. T3 my actives were Nidoqueen and Magearna, again eight attacking moves and no status move. Electivire, the Motor Drive partner the leader's bespoke tactic names, was alive and adjacent on T1.
ai_defects.chosen: MOVE_TAUNT both times (T1 into Nidoqueen, T3 into Magearna). Discharge was never selected in the whole battle.
ai_defects.why_wrong: Taunt blocks status moves, and neither target had one, so both Taunts were completely inert - the only trace either left was a 'Magearna's Taunt wore off!' message. Meanwhile the T1 board was the single best board this tactic will ever see: both of my Pokemon were Ground types, so Discharge would have dealt zero damage to me while still hitting Electivire and granting it the Motor Drive Speed boost for free. The leader's one authored bespoke tactic was available at zero cost and was passed over for a move that did nothing.
ai_defects.better: T1: MOVE_DISCHARGE, firing the authored ACTIVATE tactic at no cost. T3: an attack, or Volt Switch to pivot out of a board where Electrode had nothing useful left.
ai_defects.generalization: Two separate issues worth indexing. First, Taunt scoring against a revealed or plausibly all-attacking set: the first Taunt against an unrevealed party is a defensible prior, but the T3 repeat came after two turns in which Nidoqueen had used nothing but attacks. Second, and more important for this block, bespoke ACTIVATE tactics do not appear to be weighted above ordinary move scoring when the activation move scores badly on raw damage - which is exactly when the tactic is most valuable, because a zero-damage Discharge into a Ground board is free. Other teams carrying an ally-activation tactic of this shape should be checked for the same silence.

level_change_reasoning: Won on the first attempt with three player faints - Nidoking, Magearna and Weavile - across seven turns. By the calibration rule I was given ('Won with 2+ faints or after a real fight, keep'), this is a keep, and I have not changed any Wattson offsets. But see the calibration concern: keeping is the correct application of the rule and is still, I think, the wrong outcome for this encounter, and that judgement belongs to the main agent rather than to a lever I am capped at.
calibration_concern: The leader is levelled BELOW his own gym trainers, and it shows. Wattson's six resolve to 30/31/30/29/30/29 - his highest member is L31. Every one of the three hard rooms has at least three members at or above that: Vivian resolves to 33/33/34/29/31/32, Kirk to 32/27/31/32/29/28, Angelo to 33/28/33/29/29/29. Measured in the only currency that matters, Wattson cost me three player faints; Vivian cost three, Kirk three, Angelo four. The brief's requirement that 'Wattson must be a major step beyond the rooms' is not met - he is mid-pack, and strictly easier than Angelo. There is also a compositional reason this fight is soft that levels alone will not fix: all six members are mono-Electric or Electric/x, and four of the six are grounded, so a player who simply leads two Ground types walks in immune to the entire team's STAB. My double-Ground lead removed Electivire on turn one while taking zero damage from Electrode. The two things I would recommend the main agent weigh, neither of which I am authorized to do here: raise Wattson's whole budget by two or three so the ace sits above the rooms rather than below them, and give at least one member real coverage against a Ground lead - Magnezone's Flash Cannon and Body Press already do that job, so the gap is on the fast slots.
could_this_be_cooler: The generator-and-motor opening is a good idea and the Mega Manectric closer is genuinely well chosen - watching Lightning Rod eat two Thunderbolts and then become Intimidate the moment it transforms is the single most memorable mechanical beat in the whole gym, and the dossier predicted it exactly. The problem is that the leader currently reads as a sixth room rather than a culmination. Two concrete suggestions, neither applied. First, the tactic needs to survive its own opening: Electivire is the centrepiece and it died on turn one to two Earth Powers before Motor Drive ever existed, so the Sitrus Berry should be an Air Balloon. That single item change makes the opening board a real puzzle - the player can no longer answer both leads with Ground, has to spend a turn popping the Balloon, and during that turn the Discharge activation has somewhere to land. Second, Thundurus is the member that feels least like Wattson; it is a reachable legend doing a generic Nasty Plot job, and it spent its big turn feeding its own partner. If the slot is kept, Thunder Wave should be Taunt or Sunny Day-style disruption so Prankster priority means something even when the Electric attack is dead; if it is open to replacement, a Ground-resistant or Levitating body with non-Electric coverage would fix the composition problem and the difficulty problem in the same slot.
authored_set_legality: No legality problem found. All six prepared and ran clean, including the Manectite Mega slot 6 and Thundurus's Incarnate forme.
